hmmt-nov-2023-thm-01.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-01.body:
Let the first term be $a$ and the ratio $r$. Then $\frac{a}{1-r}=10$ and $\frac{a+4}{1-r}=15$. Dividing, $\frac{a+4}{a}=\frac32$, so $a=8$. Then $\frac{8}{1-r}=10$ gives $1-r=\frac45$, so $r=\frac15$.

**Answer: $\frac15$**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-02.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-02.body:
$RL$ is a diagonal of the square $LORE$, so the square has side $\frac{12}{\sqrt2}=6\sqrt2$. Since $FOLK$ is a rectangle, $LK\perp LO$; in the square $LE\perp LO$ too, so $K$ lies on line $LE$. Also $RE\perp LE$ with $RE=6\sqrt2$.

Then $RK^2=RE^2+EK^2$, so $121=72+EK^2$ and $EK=7$. Thus $LK=6\sqrt2\pm7$ (the two configurations: $K$ beyond $E$, or between $L$ and $E$). The area of $\triangle RKL$ is $\frac12\cdot LK\cdot RE=3\sqrt2\cdot LK$.

The product of the two areas is $(3\sqrt2)^2(6\sqrt2+7)(6\sqrt2-7)=18\cdot(72-49)=414$.

**Answer: 414**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-03.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-03.body:
**$k=8$ fails.** Take $15,0,1,0,1$ people with reputations $1,2,3,4,5$. The person with reputation $3$ and the one with reputation $5$ cannot be paired with anyone, and at most $\lfloor15/2\rfloor=7$ pairs can be formed among the $15$ people of reputation $1$.

**$k=7$ always works.** Keep forming pairs until it is impossible. Then no two remaining people share a reputation, so at most one person remains per reputation. If $4$ or more people remained, two of them would have consecutive reputations (four distinct values among $1,\dots,5$) and could be paired. So at most $3$ people remain, and at least $\frac{17-3}{2}=7$ pairs were formed.

**Answer: 7**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-04.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-04.body:
Since $LOVE$ is a rectangle, $\vec{LO}=\vec{EV}$. Let $X=R+\vec{LO}$, so $RXOL$ is a parallelogram with $RL=LO=23$, hence a rhombus: $XR=XO=23$. Also $RXVE$ is a parallelogram (since $\vec{RX}=\vec{EV}$), so $XV=RE=23$.

Thus $XR=XO=XV=23$, so $X$ is the center of the circle through $R,O,V$ and the radius is $23$.

**Answer: 23**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-05.title: Divisibility and bounds
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-05.body:
$\frac{n^3-1989}{n}=n^2-\frac{1989}{n}$ must be an integer, so $n\mid1989=3^2\cdot13\cdot17$. It must be positive, so $n^3>1989$, i.e. $n\ge13$. Being a square less than $n^2$, it is at most $(n-1)^2=n^2-2n+1$, so $\frac{1989}{n}\ge2n-1$, which gives $n\le31$.

Divisors of $1989$ in $[13,31]$: $13,17$. For $n=13$: $\frac{2197-1989}{13}=16=4^2$. For $n=17$: $\frac{4913-1989}{17}=172$, not a square. So $n=13$.

**Answer: 13**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-06.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-06.body:
Let $g(x)=(x+3)^2$ and $h(x)=x^2+9$. Then $g(1)=16=f(1)$ and $f-g\ge0$ everywhere, so $f-g$ has a double root at $x=1$: $f(x)-g(x)=c(x-1)^2$ with $c\ge0$.

Also $f-h=c(x-1)^2+(g-h)=c(x-1)^2+6x=cx^2-(2c-6)x+c\ge0$ for all $x$. For $c>0$ this needs discriminant $(2c-6)^2-4c^2=36-24c\le0$, i.e. $c\ge\frac32$ (for $c=0$ the expression $6x$ takes negative values, so $c=0$ fails).

Then $f(0)=g(0)+c=9+c\ge9+\frac32=\frac{21}{2}$, with equality at $c=\frac32$.

**Answer: $\frac{21}{2}$**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-07.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-07.body:
The grid has $4$ rows of $3$ dots. A monochromatic rectangle means two rows and two columns whose four intersection dots have the same color.

**No row is monochromatic.** Each row has two dots of one color and one of the other: $6$ possible patterns. Two rows with the same pattern share a pair of same-colored columns, giving a rectangle; two different patterns never do. So the $4$ rows must be distinct patterns: $6\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3=360$.

**Some row is all red.** Any other row with two red dots would form a rectangle with it, so each other row has at most one red dot, i.e. at least two maroon dots. An all-maroon row would then form a maroon rectangle with another row, so every other row has exactly one red dot. The three red dots must be in different columns (two rows with the red dot in the same column share the same maroon pair): $3!=6$ ways. Choosing which of the $4$ rows is all red gives $4\cdot6=24$.

**Some row is all maroon:** by symmetry $24$ (both cases cannot occur together).

Total: $360+24+24=408$. (A brute-force check over all $2^{12}$ colorings agrees.)

**Answer: 408**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-08.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-08.body:
Below $1000$ the feared numbers are $130,\dots,139$ and the numbers ending in $13$ (which are $100$ apart). Nine feared terms $n+a,\dots,n+9a$ with $a<100$ cannot fit among the numbers ending in $13$, and fitting them in $130$--$139$ forces $a=1$, $n=129$, but then $n+10a=139$ is feared. So the terms must reach four-digit numbers, and the feared numbers there are mostly of the form $13xy$.

If all of $n+a,\dots,n+9a$ lie in $1300$--$1399$, then $8a\le99$, so $a\le12$, and the smallest $n$ is $1288$ (with $a=12$: $1288,1300,1312,\dots,1396,1408$).

If instead the last term is $n+9a=1413$ (feared because it contains $13$), take $a=14$: $n=1287$ and the progression $1287,1301,1315,\dots,1399,1413,1427$ works, because $1301,\dots,1399$ all lie in $1300$--$1399$ or equal $1413$, $1287$ and $1427$ are fearless. A computer search over all $n<1287$ and $a<100$ finds no smaller $n$.

**Answer: 1287**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-09.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-09.body:
Since $NS=\frac13NO$ and $NK=\frac13NW$, we get $SK\parallel OW$ and $SK=\frac13OW$; since $NP=\frac23NO$ and $NA=\frac23NW$, $PA\parallel OW$ and $PA=\frac23OW$. Let $OW=3x$, so $SK=x$ and $PA=2x$.

Let $H$ be the distance from $N$ to $OW$. Line $SK$ is at distance $\frac23H$ from $OW$ and line $PA$ at distance $\frac13H$, so $[ESK]=\frac12\cdot x\cdot\frac23H=\frac{xH}{3}$ and $[EPA]=\frac12\cdot2x\cdot\frac13H=\frac{xH}{3}$. Both triangles have two sides ($5,6$) at $E$, so $\sin\angle SEK=\sin\angle PEA$. The angles are different (the bases $x\ne2x$), so $\angle SEK+\angle PEA=180^\circ$ and their cosines are opposite.

By the law of cosines: $x^2=61-60\cos\angle SEK$ and $4x^2=61-60\cos\angle PEA=61+60\cos\angle SEK$. Adding gives $5x^2=122$, so $x=\sqrt{\frac{122}{5}}$ and $OW=3x=\frac{3\sqrt{610}}{5}$.

**Answer: $\frac{3\sqrt{610}}{5}$**

hmmt-nov-2023-thm-10.title: Solution
hmmt-nov-2023-thm-10.body:
Let $t\in[0,2]$ be the number of full revolutions of the hour hand ($24$ hours). The minute hand is at position $12t$ and the second hand at $720t$ (in revolutions, mod $1$). The three hands form two equal angles when one hand bisects the other two, i.e. $a-2b+c\equiv0\pmod1$ for $\{a,b,c\}=\{t,12t,720t\}$:

$$697t\equiv0,\qquad 730t\equiv0,\qquad 1427t\equiv0\pmod1.$$

So $t$ is a multiple of $\frac1{697},\frac1{730}$ or $\frac1{1427}$. The numbers $697,730,1427$ are pairwise coprime, so the only common values are $t=0,1,2$ (all hands overlap). Counting $t\in[0,2]$ excluding $0,1,2$: $2\big((697-1)+(730-1)+(1427-1)\big)=5702$.

Now remove times where two hands overlap: this requires $11t$, $708t$ or $719t\equiv0\pmod 1$. Among $11,708,719,697,730,1427$ the only non-coprime pair is $708$ and $730$, with common factor $2$, giving $t=\frac12,\frac32$ (6:00 AM and PM). These $2$ are removed: $5702-2=5700$.

**Answer: 5700**
